title: America Is A Reflection Of Ancient Assyria | PART 2

sense.text: “By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom”: this is what Assyria said. Assyria gives God no glory, no honour. Done what? Destroyed the Israelites. “I have removed the bounds of the people”: the bounds of the Israelites; I removed them out of their land. “And have robbed their treasures”: their wealth. “I have put down the inhabitants like a valiant man”: like a valiant man of war.

“My hand hath found as a nest the riches of the people”: the nest eggs of the riches of the Israelites, and I took it. “There was none that moved the wing, or opened the mouth, or peeped”: no nation could speak against Assyria. That’s what the Assyrian king is saying.

“Shall the axe boast itself against him that heweth therewith?”: you got a man holding the axe and using it. The axe can’t say I did this of my own power, because the man is holding it. Likewise God is holding Assyria, using the Assyrian empire to destroy Israel, and yet they were boasting against God. “Or shall the saw magnify itself against him that shaketh it?”: God is comparing himself to the man holding the saw; he’s using Assyria as the saw. How you get hate out of that? Everybody got punished.

precepts.why: Moses prophesied about this thing. “I would scatter them into corners”: I would scatter the Israelites to the four corners of the earth. “I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”: you forget you’re the Israelites. “Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy”: the enemy meaning the nations. “Lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this”: our hand is high and God had nothing to do with it. That’s the same thing Assyria was saying here in Isaiah 10. The nations know who we are, but they give God no honour and boast themselves against him.

sense.text: “Send among his fat ones leanness”: fat means wealthy, rich, powerful. Now it’s judgment regarding Assyria. “He shall kindle a burning like the burning of a fire”: God said I’m going to send fire upon Assyria.

“And the light of Israel shall be for a fire”: right here the wording goes into the last days. It’s no longer talking so much about Assyria; he’s talking about America. “It shall burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day”: his thorns and his briers is his people. His entire system is going to be burnt up in one day. This is the problem with Christian scholars: they read the Bible like a novel. They may be okay with the history, but when it comes to prophecy they fall off the horse and cannot see with spiritual eyes.

“Both soul and body”: that’s heavy. You got to think about this type of fire, that can burn and destroy your soul. The body’s easy to understand, but the soul? “As when a standardbearer fainteth”: you’re in a war and the standard bearer has your flag, and he only drops that flag when his army’s destroyed.

“That a child may write them”: the fire is going to consume so much that the only thing left is enough for kids to be able to number. A kid’s mathematics is very low, so that’s how few trees are going to be left.

precepts.why: “Therefore shall her plagues come in one day”: America’s plagues, Babylon the Great; their plagues shall come in one day. That’s what we just read in Isaiah 10. “And she shall be utterly burned with fire”: America, Babylon the Great, shall be utterly burned with fire. “For strong is the Lord God who judgeth her.”

Here’s another one. “The Lord will come with fire”. “And with his chariots like a whirlwind”: those are his so-called UFOs. “To render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire.” “By fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.”

Something about America and the way we’ve been miseducated. When we were in Sierra Leone, some of the people there, just like here, said there’s no difference between a black Christ or a white Christ; it doesn’t matter if he’s black or white, we follow his message. Au contraire, mon frère; you’ve been miseducated. “If any man worship the beast and his image”: the beast is America, Edom, and his image is the Edomite image of Christ. If any man worship the white man, America, and that white image of Jesus, “and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand”: his political policies and religious policies in his heart, or you support it. “He shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb”: you’re going to be destroyed body and soul. “They have no rest day nor night”: that’s about your soul. So it’s wrong for our people to say it doesn’t matter if he’s black or white. We got to get that thought out of their head.

sense.text: “The remnant of Israel, and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob”: think back about the Assyrian empire. Who came after Assyria? Babylon. Were the Israelites escaped? No. Babylon conquered Assyria and took the northern kingdom, and conquered the southern kingdom, and took all 12 tribes into captivity. This whole chapter is talking about Assyria, yet it talks about us being escaped and serving the Lord in truth as a nation. That didn’t happen after Assyria, so this is going into the last days. That’s why I took us from verse 16 down into America. Those that are escaped are those of us that repent and that are caught up with the Lord. “Shall no more again stay upon him that smote them”: today the white man is smiting us, and Isaiah 30 shows how we stay upon him.

precepts.why: Those that are escaped of the house of Jacob. Verse 3 is the point, but I like verse 1 so much; it makes my teeth white. Sisters get mad at it and roll their eyes; you sisters just stay in the spirit. “In that day seven women shall take hold of one man”: this is going to be our reward. So don’t you start about the women not wanting to give a man none; you hold your stinky coochie, we’re going to get seven women at one time. “Only let us be called by thy name, to take away our reproach”: Judah be begging, but a day is going to come we ain’t got to beg no more. “In that day shall the branch of the Lord be beautiful and glorious”, “for them that are escaped of Israel”: many Black Hebrew Israelites say this is today. It’s not. As long as you still got husbands and wives fighting and stabbing each other, crack being sold on the corner, women prostituting themselves, and now men prostituting themselves, the branch of the Lord is not beautiful today. “Even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem”: a lot of Israelites are going to die, so this is only for the living.

This is how we’re going to escape. “The dead in Christ shall rise first”. “Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds”: who is the we? This includes the apostle Paul. He’s telling you about himself prophetically: in the last days I’m going to be there. Paul already saw that thing in the spirit; that’s why in Corinthians he said he went to the third heaven and saw things unlawful for him to utter. The church calls this the rapture, a Latin word that is not in the Bible; it’s the catching away. “Wherefore comfort one another with these words.”

For them that are escaped. From verse 4 down it talks about the Israelites being destroyed in 70 AD, going into captivity and being miseducated; all churches love to ignore slavery and colonialism and erase it from history when they read the Bible. Then: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days”. “And the stars shall fall from heaven”: the satellites that America, Russia and China have set up shall fall. “The powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: heavens with an s, meaning the kingdoms of the world shall shake; there’s going to be war. “Then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn”: the 12 tribes of Israel shall cry. “They shall gather together his elect from the four winds”: because, like we read in Deuteronomy 32, he would scatter them into the four corners of the earth.

Everybody says everybody’s going to be taken. Really? “When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered”: the rapture is not for all nations. We’ve been scattered here in America, England, the Caribbean islands, Africa, Iran, Iraq, and we’re going to be gathered from among the people we’ve been scattered among. “They shall dwell with confidence”: another word for confidence is faith; Paul said in Hebrews that without faith it is impossible to please God. “When I have executed judgments upon all those that despise them round about them”: that’s what the nations don’t want. Just like we got it, they’re going to get it too, and worse.

What does it mean that we shall no more again stay upon him that smote us? “Because ye despise this word”: when the Bible speaks, people say it ain’t right. “And trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon”: the white man has manipulated and perverted the ways and words of God. The Lord says man shall not lie with mankind as with womankind; America says that’s a good thing, and if you speak against it they’ll destroy your career. Use a condom: that promotes fornication, because you don’t need a condom with your spouse. LGBTQ; Democrats, then Republicans: it’s all oppression. Their religions and their politics tilt upon oppression and perverseness. “This iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall”, “whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant”: like standing in front of a wall with a big crack, about to come tumbling down; when this kingdom falls, it’s going to come at an instant. “A sherd to take fire from the hearth”: you won’t be able to warm yourself or get water from this kingdom you trust; God’s going to smash it. “In returning and rest shall ye be saved”: returning means to repent, and rest ourselves in the Bible. “In quietness and in confidence shall be your strength”: quietness means shut the hell up when the Bible is being read; confidence means faith. “And ye would not”: we want to talk; we think we know more than the prophets of old. “We will flee upon horses”: planes, trains and automobiles. Years ago at an Israelite summit of about 3,000 they were collecting money to buy a plane to escape destruction, and I asked how a plane was going to hold 3,000 of us. “Till ye be left as a beacon upon the top of a mountain, and as an ensign on an hill”: our people being jacked up is a symbol of Deuteronomy 28:15-68; we are living the curses. “Therefore will the Lord wait”: he is going to be patient till the end-time generations. “Thou shalt weep no more”: we wept from Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece and Rome, and we weep now from Spain to America, so this ain’t talking about back then.

The precept for “thou shalt weep no more” in Isaiah 30:19, to let you know it’s talking about the kingdom; based on Job 11:6, many of the scriptures we read have double meaning. “God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes”. “For the former things are passed away”: the former things are the captivities. They are going to be ended, finished, and we’re coming up to that point now.

sense.text: “Yet a remnant of them shall return”: a remnant of us shall be saved. “The consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness”: that consumption decreed is the destruction that is prophesied. This destruction is a promise; it’s a law.
“The Lord God of hosts shall make a consumption, even determined, in the midst of all the land”.

precepts.why: Psalms 91 is scary and beautiful at the same time. “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High”: the secret place of the Most High is this Bible, because the understanding of what it’s really talking about has been kept secret for ages. “The snare of the fowler”: traps set up in society, religious, political, drug traps, anything meant to keep you from the word of God. “He shall cover thee with his feathers”: those of us that repent and return to the secret place. “His truth shall be thy shield and buckler”: his law. “Nor for the arrow that flieth by day”: the ICBM missiles. “Nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday”: the Bible is prophesying when the major destruction is going to come. “A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand”: what kind of weapon could do that? Nothing but the ICBM nuclear missile, thermonuclear destruction. “Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.”

That goes with “Come up hither”. “They ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them”: this is what Christians call the rapture, but it’s only for the Israelites. “And the tenth part of the city fell”: the whole country is going to be destroyed. “And the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven”: those that are alive are going to see death all around in almost an instant, with the heat coming your way, and think the Lord has forgotten you. He’s going to gather you at the last second; that’s why we’re going to be affrighted. I’ve had dreams about that.

We’re going to be caught up, and then what? A Christian said we’re just going to stay in the air; you got to read precept upon precept. “I will bring you into the wilderness of the people”: the same wilderness we were in during the time of Moses. “Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt”: that’s the proof. “I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”: he’s going to teach us the law all over again. “I will purge out from among you the rebels”: certain men and women who were sneakily evil on this side; brothers and sisters didn’t catch their BS, but the Lord sees it. He will bring them into the wilderness just to kill them, because if you’re rebellious here you’re going to be rebellious there. “They shall not enter into the land of Israel.”

Once we’re in the wilderness, how are we going to get to the land of Israel? “The Lord shall utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea”: all that cosmetic talk, that talk of oppression. “And shall smite it in the seven streams, and make men go over dryshod”: he’s going to part the rivers once again, and we’re going to walk across on dry land, just like during the time of Moses. “Like as it was to Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.”

The consumption. “Two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein”: and some of the third that’s left, God said I’m going to kill them on the other side. When I read this I said, Lord, please don’t let me be one of them.

sense.text: “O my people that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid of the Assyrian”: remember we’re talking about the last days. It’s the same with us today: be not afraid of America, Babylon the Great. “He shall smite thee with a rod”: just as Assyria smote us with the rod, America is doing the same thing. That’s what the SPLC is about; they put out two articles in one week about us, to sully us so our people will never repent. “After the manner of Egypt”: just like ancient Egypt did. One of the brothers in North Carolina has a public job, and now they’re trying to get him fired for being affiliated with a hate group. Those of you with high-profile jobs don’t have to be in the forefront; they did the same thing with Marcus Garvey and the UNIA. It’s best to be an entrepreneur if you can. Don’t be afraid just because we’re oppressed. In conclusion, America reflects ancient Assyria. Be not afraid, brothers and sisters: many things are going to come our way, but these things must come to pass for us to inherit eternal life. We must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom, men and women alike.

precepts.why: About America. “Take up this proverb against the king of Babylon”: the king of Babylon is the United States of America. “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!”: yes, America is the oppressor, and yes, they are the golden city, the most glorious kingdom on earth right now; that’s why everybody wants to come here. “He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke”: he ain’t stopping. All these things he set up throughout his system are traps for our people; that’s how he’s smiting us. It’s saying the same thing as Isaiah 10:24, but more specific about Babylon. “Is persecuted, and none hindereth”: when the persecution comes to Babylon, nobody’s going to be able to stop it.

Another way they’re smiting us. “Hindered their building”: they want to hinder us building the 12 tribes of Israel and travelling to these places to build them up. “And by their secret plots”: anything that happens with any one of you members, they don’t blame the individual; they blame the organisation. Then they sully our reputation in the eyes of our people so that our people will not repent. In the forefront you got the SPLC, followed by the FBI. “Popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building”.

You’ll read 1 Esdras and say it’s just talking about the actual building back then. No; remember Job 11:6, his words of wisdom are double. “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house”: we are a spiritual house, so when it says they hindered the finishing of the building, we can look at it with spiritual eyes. Christianity teaches you to read the Bible like a novel with one layer; we read it with double vision, spiritual eyes and earthly eyes.

The last verse to remember. “So shall they fear the name of the Lord from the west”: this is the western hemisphere; his name is the word of God. “And his glory from the rising of the sun”: the east, where we’re over there teaching. “When the enemy shall come in like a flood”: the enemy is going to come against us, because the greatest nation on earth is resurrecting now. “The Spirit of the Lord shall lift up a standard against him”: don’t worry, don’t fear. “And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob”. So don’t fear, Israel.

sense.text: “For yet a very little while, and the indignation shall cease”.

“According to the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb”: when Gideon destroyed Midian; he’s going to raise up men against them and slaughter them the same way. “As his rod was upon the sea, so shall he lift it up after the manner of Egypt”: like when Moses lifted up his rod.

“His burden shall be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck”: this is talking about these last days. “And the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing”: the anointing is Christ. The yoke of bondage is going to be broken off of us because of the anointing. The anointing begins with Christ giving it to us, and it translates to the Israelite studying, praying and applying what is written, and that applying is very difficult for men and women for some reason.

precepts.why: A precept for the indignation ceasing. “Fear not; for thou shalt not be ashamed”: if the curses in Deuteronomy 28 came to pass, you better believe the blessings will surely come. “Neither be thou confounded”: don’t be confused. “For thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth”: in Egypt, and under Assyria, Babylon, Greece and Rome. “The reproach of thy widowhood”: God cut us off from being his wife; we were his wife, like another scripture says, I am married unto you. “For thy Maker is thine husband”: that’s the evidence; that’s what Christ coming was all about. “The God of the whole earth shall he be called”: we’re going to subdue all nations and make them worship the Most High. “For a small moment have I forsaken thee”: we’ve been here 400 years, really from 70 AD till now, and to us it seems like forever, but he calls it a small moment. “In a little wrath I hid my face”: he’s just mad a little bit. “This is as the waters of Noah unto me”: the same way he promised Noah not to destroy the earth with water anymore, he promises not to be wroth with the Israelites no more. “The mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed”: the nations, the kingdoms. “But my kindness shall not depart from thee”.

Explaining the anointing. “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”. “And to anoint the most Holy”: to anoint the most holy is Christ. He is the most holy that was anointed first and foremost.

“But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you”. “As the same anointing teacheth you of all things”: when you come in this truth and repent, the anointing begins to come upon you, and it takes time; not a day, not two weeks, not even a year. The disciples walked with the Son of God about three years before they got the anointing, so it’s going to be a little longer with us. It comes through trial and error, studying, praying and applying, and after some time you’ll be able to open a book and explain the verses both on the surface and in the spiritual context.

He’s going to break the yoke off our neck. “The Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. “And they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors”: we shall rule over our oppressors; that’s what he means by breaking the yoke. “From the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve”: the hard bondage is that heavy yoke Isaiah spoke of in chapter 10.
